preconditions.description: The tree size n and query count q are within the specified bounds.

preconditions.expression: len(parent_nodes) == n - 1 and all(1 <= int(p) <= n for p in parent_nodes)
preconditions.description: The parent list has exactly n-1 elements, each representing a valid parent node index.

preconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(v) <= n for v in queries)
preconditions.description: Each query node index v is within the valid range of node indices.

postconditions.description: The output contains exactly one centroid index per query.

postconditions.expression: all(1 <= int(line.strip()) <= n for line in output_lines)
postconditions.description: Each output centroid index is a valid node index.

postconditions.expression: all(any(is_centroid(v, subtree_size, subtree_nodes) for v in subtree_nodes) for v, subtree_size, subtree_nodes in zip(queries, subtree_sizes, subtree_node_lists))
postconditions.description: For each query, the output centroid is a valid centroid of the corresponding subtree, where is_centroid(v, size, nodes) is true if removing v splits the subtree into components each of size <= size/2.

candidate_issues.task_evidence: Centroid of a tree (or a subtree) is a node, such that if we erase it from the tree, the maximum size of the connected component will be at least two times smaller than the size of the initial tree (or a subtree).
